name: Magnetoreception Navigation Complex
description: Introduces cryptochrome proteins and iron-oxide nanocrystals into the ethmoid bone and retinal cells, granting the user an innate sense of magnetic north and geomagnetic field variations. The user always knows which direction they're facing, can sense their approximate latitude by field inclination, and can detect magnetic anomalies in their environment — buried metal, electromagnetic equipment, and geological features. The sensation is subtle — a gentle 'pull' toward magnetic north that becomes second nature within weeks. Users report that losing the sense (in magnetically shielded rooms or near strong magnets) is disorienting in the same way that sudden darkness is disorienting to a sighted person. Zheng-Dao Bioelectric offers an enhanced version that includes sensitivity to artificial magnetic fields, allowing users to navigate by the electromagnetic signatures of GLMZ's infrastructure.
source_organism: Columba livia (rock pigeon), Chelonia mydas (green sea turtle, magnetic navigation genes)
procedure: Cranial retroviral injection targeting ethmoid bone and retinal cells, 2 sessions
reversibility: Partially reversible; iron-oxide deposits persist even after protein suppression
side_effects: Strong magnets cause headaches and disorientation
MRI machines are excruciatingly painful and potentially dangerous
Metal detectors give false positives from iron-oxide deposits
Rare: migraine-like episodes during geomagnetic storms
social_perception: Niche and respected. Navigation-profession users (couriers, explorers, infrastructure workers) swear by it. The modification is invisible, which means it carries no social stigma — no one knows you have it unless you tell them.
story_hooks: A Compass Blood courier navigates GLMZ's labyrinthine infrastructure by magnetic signature alone — until a section of the city's magnetic landscape shifts overnight, and they discover someone is rebuilding the underground
A Pigeon Brain user begins sensing magnetic signatures that don't match any known infrastructure — something large and metallic is moving beneath the city
